t: Day nine of the rain. I have marked the same quiz four times. It is now perfect.
(to frozen Gus) Last time we heard an r, buddy. This time we hear the whole word.
The Rewinder can reach the night of the freeze. Getting home again is the problem.
The Undefined took the ground there. If it takes our line too, we're stuck in the past.
So I built a track layer. Give it a rule, and it lays a line. Any line we can write, we can ride.
We're going to build our own road? Out of MATHS?
Out of maths.
Be home by dinner. And if you see me in the past, tell me my tie is fine.
The ground's going! Effie, the line's going with it!
Hold on to something. Anything!
We're stranded. No ground. That light is the clock tower. We lay a track to it.
The track layer has one rule loaded. Y equals two x, plus one.
Plus one! So start at one! One across, right there on the bottom. Lay it!
(dangling over the fog) WHY is there no floor in the past?!
Your track missed the tower. The start isn't on the across line. The start is where x is zero.
(from somewhere below) Where x is zero? ...So the start is always mine.
Put zero in. Two times zero is zero. Plus one is one. The start is zero across, one up.
Now the step. The two is the step. Over one, up two. Over one, up two.
One, three, five, seven, nine. Up two every time. That's going straight to the tower!
Two landing pads at three across. The Undefined left a fake. Only one is on our line.
Test it. Put three in. Two times three is six, plus one is seven. The pad at seven is real.
So the one at eight is a FAKE! Ha! Crumble, fake pad!
(climbing out of the fog) Found you. The tower's up high. The way home goes down.
The next rule is y equals minus two x, plus eight. Start at eight. Step: minus two.
Minus two? We're going DOWN the stairs this time?
Over one, down two. Eight, six, four, two... zero.
Four steps from eight down to zero. So the track meets the floor at four across. Right at the station.
Where a line meets the floor, y is zero. Count the steps down to it.
Good evening. Day nine of the rain. Townspeople are building boats. The forecast still says zero percent.
We have a caller.
(on the phone) Chip! It's Marcus. I'm calling from nowhere.
...And how is the weather in nowhere?
(on the phone) Foggy. No floor. We're making our own road out of maths.
Caller, that is the most sensible thing anyone has said all week.
Next stop, the old bridge. A gentle ramp this time. Y equals one half x, plus two.
One half? You can't go up HALF a step. My legs don't do halves.
Then don't go over one. Go over two. Half of two is one. Over two, up one.
Start at two. Over two, up one. Over two, up one. Over two, up one.
Two, three, four, five. Lands on the bridge. My legs approve.
The last track. No rule this time. Just two glowing marks on the line home.
The first mark is at zero across. So that's the start. Three.
From one mark to the other: over two, up four. Four over two is two. The step is two.
Start three, step two. Y equals two x, plus three.
Check it on home. Four across: two times four is eight, plus three is eleven. Home is eleven up. It's on the line!
We're home! I can feel the floor! I love the floor!
Start where x is zero. Then step. That's all a line is.
But we still only saw the night from outside. To reach the moment itself, we need to know exactly when.
(staring at the window) Gus? ...Did you write that?
Three x plus four is twenty-five. It's not a line. It's a question. What's x?
Then next time, we solve for it. And we arrive at the exact second.
Coo.
So am I a sidekick yet? I built a ROAD.
No.
